title: [VSC-1] VS Code: notify on task status transitions, matching JetBrains
description:
Epic epic-aabc654d (VS Code works + plugin reuse), sliced by task-a3e414a3 (VSC-0); decision doc docs/plans/2026-11-02-vscode-reuse.md. First wave: no dependencies, files disjoint from the other first-wave rows.

Objective: VS Code tells the human nothing when a task needs them; JetBrains does. Port JetBrains' rule exactly. Source of truth: moe-jetbrains MoeMessageDispatcher.kt, the `"TASK_UPDATED", "TASK_CREATED"` branch (notify only when the cached task's status differs from the frame's status; an uncached task counts as different), and MoeNotificationService.kt for the texts:
- AWAITING_APPROVAL: info, title "Plan Awaiting Approval", message `Task "<title>" has a plan ready for review`, action "View Task".
- BLOCKED: warning, "Task Blocked", `Task "<title>" is blocked and needs attention`, action "View Task".
- REVIEW: info, "Task Ready for Review", `Task "<title>" is ready for code review`, action "View Task".
- DONE: info, "Task Completed", `Task "<title>" has been marked as done`, no action.
Every other status, a same-status frame, STATE_SNAPSHOT and TASK_DELETED never notify. JetBrains' notifyConnectionLost/notifyConnectionRestored are never called, so they are not part of parity. VS Code shows one line, `<title>: <message>`; "View Task" runs `moe.openTaskDetail` with the task id.

Seam (verified at 882a4c39): MoeDaemonClient.handleMessage fires onTaskUpdated(payload) for TASK_UPDATED and TASK_CREATED BEFORE it writes the payload into currentState (case 'TASK_UPDATED'), so a listener reads the cached status from client.currentState. No MoeDaemonClient.ts change is needed; another first-wave row (VSC-6) owns that file.

Deliverable: new moe-vscode/src/util/TaskNotifier.ts with a pure `taskNotification(previousStatus, task)` decision and a `registerTaskNotifier(client, window, commands)` returning a Disposable; moe-vscode/src/extension.ts registers it in activate() and pushes it to context.subscriptions; new moe-vscode/tests/task-notifier.test.cjs (ts.transpileModule + node:vm, a require map that throws on any undeclared module; pattern in tests/managed-vm.test.cjs).

Not in scope: a mute setting (package.json belongs to first-wave row VSC-2), connection notices, plan-approval refusal notices (PlanReviewPanel owns them), any change to MoeDaemonClient.ts, package.json or media/.

Verification (GLOBAL rail: never npm in the shared checkout): `git archive HEAD` of the whole repo into a fresh directory outside the checkout, overlay this task's files, then in <snapshot>/moe-vscode run `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test` under `env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin` (mem:gotcha-vscode-gate-from-wsl). Baseline at 882a4c39: lint 0, compile 0, 388 tests, 384 pass, 4 skip, 0 fail.
definitionOfDone: moe-vscode/tests/task-notifier.test.cjs runs the real TaskNotifier.ts (ts.transpileModule + node:vm, a require map that throws on any undeclared module) and asserts the exact kind, title, message and action (command moe.openTaskDetail with the task id, or none for DONE) for AWAITING_APPROVAL, BLOCKED, REVIEW and DONE transitions.
The same test asserts no notification for: a same-status frame, a cached task moving to PLANNING or WORKING, an uncached task arriving in BACKLOG, an ARCHIVED frame, and a STATE_SNAPSHOT.

With a fake client that fires onTaskUpdated before it updates currentState (as MoeDaemonClient does), a WORKING to REVIEW frame shows exactly one notification, an immediately repeated REVIEW frame shows none, and after the notifier is disposed no frame notifies.

moe-vscode/src/extension.ts registers the notifier in activate() and pushes its Disposable into context.subscriptions; the task's diff leaves moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts, moe-vscode/package.json and moe-vscode/media/ unchanged.

In a git-archive snapshot of HEAD plus this diff, `cd moe-vscode && npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test` exits 0 with 0 failures and more passing tests than the 384-pass baseline.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD, tests first: create moe-vscode/tests/task-notifier.test.cjs and see it fail (TaskNotifier.ts missing) before step 2. Read mem:gotcha-vscode-vm-test-harness (vm realms, driving the real client) and mem:gotcha-vscode-panel-strict-require-map first.
LOADER for TaskNotifier.ts: copy the tests/managed-vm.test.cjs loader - ts.transpileModule (CommonJS, ES2020), then vm.runInThisContext('(function (exports, module, require) {' + code + '\n})') with a require that throws `TaskNotifier.ts must not require ${name}` for EVERY name (the module uses only `import type`). runInThisContext keeps returned objects in the test realm, so assert.deepEqual (node:assert/strict) works on taskNotification results.
Fixtures: task(status, more) = { id: 'task-1', title: 'Ship it', status, ...more }; VIEW = { label: 'View Task', command: 'moe.openTaskDetail', taskId: 'task-1' }.
(A) DoD 1, exact texts, pure decision:
- taskNotification('PLANNING', task('AWAITING_APPROVAL')) deepEquals { kind: 'info', title: 'Plan Awaiting Approval', message: 'Task "Ship it" has a plan ready for review', action: VIEW }
- ('WORKING', BLOCKED) -> { kind: 'warning', title: 'Task Blocked', message: 'Task "Ship it" is blocked and needs attention', action: VIEW }
- ('WORKING', REVIEW) -> { kind: 'info', title: 'Task Ready for Review', message: 'Task "Ship it" is ready for code review', action: VIEW }
- ('REVIEW', DONE) -> { kind: 'info', title: 'Task Completed', message: 'Task "Ship it" has been marked as done' } with NO action key (strict deepEqual tells a missing key from action: undefined)
- (undefined, REVIEW) -> the REVIEW object (an uncached task counts as different).
(B) DoD 2, never notify: ('REVIEW', REVIEW), ('BLOCKED', BLOCKED), ('BACKLOG', PLANNING), ('AWAITING_APPROVAL', WORKING), (undefined, BACKLOG), ('DONE', ARCHIVED) each return undefined.
(C) DoD 2+3, fake client. fakeClient(tasks) has:
- currentState { tasks };
- onTaskUpdated(listener), returning { dispose } that removes the listener;
- frame(t): fires the listeners FIRST (over a copy), THEN writes t into currentState.tasks (replace by id, push if new, drop on ARCHIVED). This is the order of MoeDaemonClient.handleMessage case 'TASK_UPDATED';
- snapshot(tasks): replaces currentState and fires nothing (STATE_SNAPSHOT only fires onStateChanged).
Recorder window: showInformationMessage/showWarningMessage push { kind: 'info'|'warning', line, items } and return Promise.resolve(answer), answer settable. commands.executeCommand pushes [command, ...args] and returns a settable promise.
Sequence: seed [task('WORKING')], register.
1. A REVIEW frame records exactly [{ kind: 'info', line: 'Task Ready for Review: Task "Ship it" is ready for code review', items: ['View Task'] }].
2. The same REVIEW frame again adds nothing; a WORKING frame adds nothing.
3. snapshot([task('DONE')]) adds nothing; then snapshot([task('WORKING')]).
4. dispose(), then a DONE frame (one that WOULD notify) adds nothing.
Separate rows:
- a BLOCKED frame is kind 'warning' with items ['View Task'];
- DONE is 'info' with items [];
- with currentState undefined (before the first snapshot) a REVIEW frame records nothing (JetBrains returns early when currentState() is null).
(D) Action:
- answer 'View Task': after `await new Promise(r => setImmediate(r))` the commands are exactly [['moe.openTaskDetail', 'task-1']];
- answer undefined: [];
- a DONE notice (no button): [];
- executeCommand returning Promise.reject(new Error('boom')): after the flush, one more { kind: 'warning', line: 'Moe: could not open task task-1: boom', items: [] } is recorded.
(E) Link neutralization. Title '[Approve](command:workbench.action.terminal.sendSequence?%7B%7D)'. LINK_REGEX = /\[([^\]]+)\]\(((?:https?:\/\/|command:|file:)[^\)\s]+)(?: (["'])(.+?)(\3))?\)/i, copied from microsoft/vscode src/vs/base/common/linkedText.ts minus the g flag; cite it in a comment.
- assert.match(title, LINK_REGEX): the fixture is live.
- The REVIEW notice's message equals 'Task "[Approve] (command:workbench.action.terminal.sendSequence?%7B%7D)" is ready for code review'.
- assert.doesNotMatch(recorded line, LINK_REGEX).
(F) Real-client seam guard. Transpile src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts and run it in vm.createContext the way tests/plan-approval-client.test.cjs createHarness does. Copy RecordingEventEmitter, the vscode stub (EventEmitter, window.createOutputChannel/showErrorMessage, workspace.getConfiguration -> { get: () => false } so no reconnect timer) and the vscode/ws/child_process/fs/path/net require switch. Never require() that test file: it registers its own tests at load.
Register the real notifier on new MoeDaemonClient('extension') and feed frames through client['handleMessage'](JSON.stringify(frame)):
1. STATE_SNAPSHOT { tasks: [task-1 WORKING], epics: [] } -> 0 recorded
2. TASK_UPDATED task-1 REVIEW -> exactly 1
3. the same frame again -> 1
4. TASK_DELETED task-1 -> 1
5. TASK_CREATED task-2 BACKLOG -> 1
6. STATE_SNAPSHOT [task-2 DONE] -> 1
7. TASK_UPDATED task-2 AWAITING_APPROVAL -> 2
Put client.dispose() in finally. This row goes red if a later edit to handleMessage caches a frame before firing onTaskUpdated (sibling rows VSC-6 and VSC-12 edit that file). Compare only test-realm strings and arrays: vm-realm objects fail strict deepEqual.

implementationPlan.description:
Create moe-vscode/src/util/TaskNotifier.ts so step 1's tests pass. Use type-only imports only: `import type * as vscode from 'vscode'`, `import type { MoeDaemonClient } from '../services/MoeDaemonClient'`, `import type { Task, TaskStatus } from '../types/moe'`. The transpiled module then has zero require() calls, so the esbuild bundle and every strict vm require map are unaffected. The planner type-checked these exact Pick signatures under TS 6.0.3 (0 diagnostics), and vscode.window, vscode.commands and the client all fit them.
1. `export interface TaskNotification { kind: 'info' | 'warning'; title: string; message: string; action?: { label: string; command: string; taskId: string } }`
2. `export function taskNotification(previousStatus: TaskStatus | undefined, task: Task): TaskNotification | undefined` ports the JetBrains MoeMessageDispatcher.kt 'TASK_UPDATED', 'TASK_CREATED' rule:
- return undefined when previousStatus === task.status;
- otherwise switch on task.status with the MoeNotificationService.kt texts:
  - AWAITING_APPROVAL: info, 'Plan Awaiting Approval', `Task "${name}" has a plan ready for review`
  - BLOCKED: warning, 'Task Blocked', `Task "${name}" is blocked and needs attention`
  - REVIEW: info, 'Task Ready for Review', `Task "${name}" is ready for code review`
  - these three carry action { label: 'View Task', command: 'moe.openTaskDetail', taskId: task.id }
  - DONE: info, 'Task Completed', `Task "${name}" has been marked as done`; omit the action key, do not set it to undefined
  - default: undefined.
name = String(task.title).replace(/\]\(/g, '] ('), with a one-line comment. Why: VS Code renders [label](command:...) in notification text as a clickable command link (linkedText.ts LINK_REGEX, opened with allowCommands: true), and task titles are agent-written. A title without '](' is unchanged, so the JetBrains texts hold exactly.
3. `export function registerTaskNotifier(client: Pick<MoeDaemonClient, 'currentState' | 'onTaskUpdated'>, window: Pick<typeof vscode.window, 'showInformationMessage' | 'showWarningMessage'>, commands: Pick<typeof vscode.commands, 'executeCommand'>): vscode.Disposable` returns the client.onTaskUpdated(listener) subscription itself: disposing it unsubscribes, and nothing else needs cleanup. The listener:
- `const state = client.currentState; if (!state || !task) return;` (JetBrains ignores TASK_* frames until the first STATE_SNAPSHOT)
- `n = taskNotification(state.tasks.find(t => t.id === task.id)?.status, task)`. This reads the OLD status because MoeDaemonClient.handleMessage fires onTaskUpdated BEFORE it caches the frame (verified at 241ac770; step 1 (F) guards it). Never write currentState.
- If there is no n, return. Otherwise show `${n.title}: ${n.message}`: showWarningMessage for 'warning', else showInformationMessage. Pass 'View Task' as the only item when n.action exists (type items as string[]).
- When the pick equals the action label, return commands.executeCommand(n.action.command, n.action.taskId).
Error handling: end that show->execute chain with .then(undefined, (err: unknown) => window.showWarningMessage(`Moe: could not open task ${task.id}: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`)), because Thenable has no .catch. A failed open (command gone after deactivate, panel creation throws) then reaches the human as a warning, not an unhandled rejection in the extension host. No timers, no other state, no setting: a mute setting needs package.json, which VSC-2 owns.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
VS Code tells the human when a task needs them, using JetBrains' rule. A TASK_UPDATED or TASK_CREATED frame whose status differs from the cached task's (an uncached task counts as different) shows one notification, `<title>: <message>`:
- AWAITING_APPROVAL: info, 'Plan Awaiting Approval: Task "<t>" has a plan ready for review'
- BLOCKED: warning, 'Task Blocked: Task "<t>" is blocked and needs attention'
- REVIEW: info, 'Task Ready for Review: Task "<t>" is ready for code review'
- DONE: info, 'Task Completed: Task "<t>" has been marked as done'
The first three carry a 'View Task' button that runs moe.openTaskDetail with the task id; DONE has none.
Nothing is shown for any other status, a same-status frame, STATE_SNAPSHOT, TASK_DELETED, or a frame before the first STATE_SNAPSHOT. '](' in a title becomes '] (', so a title cannot plant a clickable command link. A failed View Task open shows as a warning. Disposing the notifier (extension deactivate) stops all notices.
acceptanceCriteria: DoD 1: tests/task-notifier.test.cjs loads the real TaskNotifier.ts (transpileModule + node:vm, a require that throws on every module) and asserts the exact kind, title, message and action (moe.openTaskDetail + task id; none for DONE) for AWAITING_APPROVAL, BLOCKED, REVIEW and DONE.

DoD 2: the same file asserts no notification for a same-status frame, a cached task moving to PLANNING or WORKING, an uncached task arriving in BACKLOG, an ARCHIVED frame, and a STATE_SNAPSHOT (fake client and the real MoeDaemonClient).

DoD 3: with a fake client that fires onTaskUpdated before updating currentState, WORKING->REVIEW shows exactly one notification, an immediate repeat shows none, and after dispose() a frame that would otherwise notify shows none.
DoD 4: extension.ts registers the notifier in activate() and pushes its Disposable into context.subscriptions; the task diff leaves MoeDaemonClient.ts, package.json and media/ unchanged.
DoD 5: checkRefs[0] exits 0 with 0 failures and more than 384 passing tests.

Every show/execute Thenable chain ends in a rejection handler.
A title without '](' yields the JetBrains text byte for byte.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) Put the rule inside MoeDaemonClient.handleMessage: rejected. VSC-6 owns that file this wave, and a separate pure module is testable without a socket.
2) Diff snapshots in onStateChanged: rejected. It fires after the cache write (the old status is gone) and also on STATE_SNAPSHOT, which must never notify.
3) Fake-client-only test: kept, per DoD 3, plus one real-client row (F). The fire-before-cache seam lives in a file that VSC-6 and VSC-12 will edit, and row F turns a silent breakage into a red test.
4) Mute setting or connection notices: out of scope. package.json belongs to VSC-2, and JetBrains never calls notifyConnectionLost/Restored.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- No onTaskUpdated subscriber exists before this task, and the VS Code EventEmitter delivers synchronously, so the listener reads the pre-frame cache.
- vm realms: objects created inside vm.createContext fail strict deepEqual against test-realm objects; strings cross freely (mem:gotcha-vscode-vm-test-harness). runInThisContext keeps TaskNotifier's results in the test realm.
- Thenable has no .catch, so use .then(undefined, handler).
- src/ has no console use, and MoeDaemonClient's log() is module-private, so the user-visible warning is the error path.
- tests/daemon-json-cap.test.cjs regex-matches extension.ts's MoeDaemonClient import line.

planningNotes.risks:
(a) Strict deepEqual: DONE must omit the action key, not set it to undefined.
(b) The dispose row must use a frame that WOULD notify, or it passes vacuously.
(c) Cross-realm: in row F compare only recorded strings and arrays built in the test realm.
(d) Row F must stub workspace.getConfiguration().get() -> false, or a reconnect timer holds node:test open.
(e) The '](' -> '] (' rewrite is an intentional, commented divergence from JetBrains (a command-link guard) and is invisible for normal titles.
(f) Peer rows (VSC-2 package.json, VSC-6 MoeDaemonClient.ts) may have dirty edits in the shared tree. The gate overlays only this task's three files onto HEAD, so they cannot leak in; never stage them.
